previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, GERD, and anxiety was admitted for two days of constant epigastric discomfort described as similar to her pre-bypass symptoms. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out by normal EKGs, undetectable troponin levels on two occasions, and a normal exercise stress test. Her symptoms improved with pantoprazole, supporting a diagnosis of dyspepsia. She was found to have elevated blood pressure during admission, prompting an increase in lisinopril from 5mg to 10mg. Her anxiety, exacerbated by significant social stressors including her grandson’s uncertain living situation, was addressed with ongoing therapy and social work support. She remained stable throughout her stay, was discharged home on updated medications, and advised to follow up with her cardiologist and primary care provider.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yr F with hx of CAD s/p CABG, HLD, HTN, hypothroid, and 
osteoporosis who presents today with weakness.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Proximal weakness: Subacute presentation of weakness, worse at 
night and proximal on exam with right lid ptosis (and exotropia) 
in the setting of a normal CK. Question of myasthenia ___. 
___ is possible as well. She is also rather Cushingoid 
in habitus with ? fat pad, cataracts, osteoporosis. 
Non-inflammatory myopathies are certainly plausible. Her ESR and 
CRP came back elevated. Endocrine myopathies were considered but 
her AM and ___ cortisol were normal, she was found mildly 
hypothyroid, PTH unremarkable and her acetylcholine receptor 
antibodies returned negative (though this does not rule out MG). 
It was thought that the patient might have a myopathy that did 
not elevate CK and could benefit from an outpatient workup with 
neuromuscular neurology.

# UTI: She presented with frequency without dysuria. Cultures 
were drawn (which returned negative) and she was given a 7 day 
course of cipro, beginning on ___.  

INACTIVE ISSUES:
# Anemia: normocytic, nl RDW. Iron is low without evidence of 
bleeding or hemolysis.
# High lactate: etiology unclear as there is no evidence of 
hemolysis or ongoing ischemia. She is clearly not septic. She 
does not take metformin.
# hypothyroid: TSH mildly elevated but this may be related to 
acute phase reactant rather than management of hypothyroid. 
Synthroid was continued. 
# hx of CAD - continued metoprolol, ASA
# osteoporosis - continued raloxifene, Ca, vitamin D
# GERD - continued PPI 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
# WEAKNESS: It was thought that this could be consistent with 
any number of myopathies. Her condition was good enough to 
permit a safe outpatient workup. 

# HYPOTHYROID: Synthroid may need to be adjusted as her TSH was 
mildly elevated, although this may have been an acute phase 
reactant in the setting of elevated CRP and ESR.
